## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the operation, calibration, and maintenance
of the Invitrogen Qubit 4 Fluorometer. The Qubit uses fluorescent dyes
that bind selectively to the target molecule (dsDNA, ssDNA, RNA, or
protein), providing more accurate quantification than UV absorbance
methods, especially at low concentrations or when contaminants are
present. For the role of Qubit measurements within the DNA extraction
workflow, see
[SOP-L700 DNA Extraction](SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd).


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** All use of the Qubit 4 Fluorometer in the EA Program
  laboratory, including dsDNA Broad Range (BR), dsDNA High Sensitivity
  (HS), RNA, and protein assays
- **Does not apply to:** UV-Vis spectrophotometric quantification (see
  [SOP-L212](SOP-L212-nanodrop-spectrophotometer.qmd)), Turner Designs
  fluorometry for chlorophyll or other environmental analytes (see
  [SOP-L203](SOP-L203-trilogy-fluorometer.qmd))
- **Location:** Instrument bench, SGM 133


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, authorize instrument access    |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain reagent inventory, schedule service |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report malfunctions        |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Qubit reagent concentrate contains DMSO. Avoid skin
  contact; review the SDS before handling.
- **Biological:** Samples may contain hazardous biological material.
  Treat all samples as potentially infectious.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves

### Emergency Procedures

For chemical splashes, flush with water for at least 15 minutes and
consult the SDS. For biological spills, clean per
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd).

| Qubit dsDNA BR Assay Kit              | Q32850        | Room temperature |
| Qubit dsDNA HS Assay Kit              | Q32851        | Room temperature |
| Qubit assay tubes (0.5 mL, thin-wall) | Q32856        | Room temperature |
| Nuclease-free water                   | Various       | Room temperature |

::: {.callout-note}
Use only the thin-wall 0.5 mL Qubit assay tubes (Cat. Q32856). Standard
microcentrifuge tubes are not optically compatible and will produce
inaccurate readings.
:::


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Selecting the Assay

Choose the assay based on expected concentration:

| Assay         | Detection Range          | When to Use                     |
|:--------------|:-------------------------|:--------------------------------|
| dsDNA BR      | 2--1,000 ng              | Most soil/sediment extractions  |
| dsDNA HS      | 0.2--100 ng              | Low-yield samples (e.g., water filters, dilute extracts) |
| RNA BR / HS   | See kit documentation    | RNA quantification              |
| Protein       | See kit documentation    | Protein quantification          |

### 6.2 Preparing the Working Solution

1. Calculate the volume of working solution needed: 200 uL per assay
   tube (all samples plus 2 standards)
2. Dilute the Qubit reagent concentrate 1:200 in Qubit buffer. For
   example, for 10 tubes: 10 uL reagent + 1,990 uL buffer = 2,000 uL
   total.
3. Vortex briefly to mix

::: {.callout-important}
Prepare the working solution fresh for each session. Do not store
diluted working solution.
:::

### 6.3 Preparing Standards

1. Label two Qubit assay tubes: **Std 1** and **Std 2**
2. Add 190 uL of working solution to each tube
3. Add 10 uL of Standard 1 to the first tube and 10 uL of Standard 2
   to the second tube
4. Vortex each tube briefly (2--3 seconds)

### 6.4 Preparing Samples

1. Label one Qubit assay tube per sample
2. Add 198 uL of working solution to each tube
3. Add 2 uL of sample (DNA extract, RNA, or protein solution) to the
   corresponding tube
4. Vortex each tube briefly (2--3 seconds)

::: {.callout-tip}
The sample volume can range from 1--20 uL as long as the total volume
in each tube equals 200 uL (adjust the working solution volume
accordingly). Using 2 uL of sample minimizes consumption of precious
extracts.
:::

### 6.5 Incubation

1. Incubate all tubes (standards and samples) at room temperature for
   2 minutes
2. Do not incubate for longer than 30 minutes; fluorescence signal
   decays over time

### 6.6 Calibration

1. On the Qubit home screen, select the appropriate assay (e.g.,
   **dsDNA Broad Range**)
2. Tap **Read Standards**
3. Insert the Std 1 tube, close the lid, and tap **Read**
4. When prompted, insert the Std 2 tube, close the lid, and tap **Read**
5. Verify that the calibration is accepted (green checkmark). If it
   fails, prepare fresh standards and repeat.

### 6.7 Reading Samples

1. Tap **Run Samples**
2. Set the sample volume to match the volume of sample added (e.g.,
   2 uL)
3. Set the output units (ng/uL is standard for DNA extracts)
4. Insert the sample tube, close the lid, and tap **Read**
5. Record the concentration (ng/uL, corrected for dilution by the
   instrument)
6. Repeat for all samples

### 6.8 Data Export

1. Export results via USB or Wi-Fi to the designated project folder
2. Use a consistent file-naming convention:
   `YYYY-MM-DD_Qubit_ProjectName.csv`
3. Record results in the lab notebook and/or project data sheet

### 6.9 Shutdown and Daily Maintenance

1. Remove all tubes from the instrument
2. Wipe the sample chamber with a lint-free tissue if any liquid was
   spilled
3. Close the lid
4. Dispose of used assay tubes (see Section 8)


## 7. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Run fresh standards at the beginning of each session; do not rely on
  a previous calibration
- Standards must be within the acceptable range indicated by the
  instrument (green checkmark)
- If a sample reads "Out of Range," re-prepare it using the other assay
  sensitivity (e.g., switch from BR to HS for low-concentration samples)
- Acceptable DNA yield from 0.25 g of soil: typically 1--20 ng/uL in a
  100 uL elution, depending on soil type
- If the NanoDrop and Qubit concentrations disagree by more than a
  factor of two, the NanoDrop reading is likely inflated by
  contaminants; trust the Qubit value for downstream planning

*TBD -- establish a periodic performance check using Qubit DNA standards
of known concentration.*


## 8. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Used Qubit assay tubes        | Standard trash (rinse if biohazardous)   |
| Leftover working solution     | Standard drain (dilute DMSO, non-hazardous at this concentration) |
| Pipette tips                  | Standard trash (or biohazard if samples are hazardous) |

## 10. Training Record

Before using the Qubit independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Observe a trained operator demonstrate standard preparation,
   calibration, sample reading, and data export
4. Perform a practice session (calibration plus at least 5 samples)
   under supervision
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
